data.name: Ezekiel Delacroix
data.concept: The ex-cop New Orleans forgot to stop

edges.name: GLOBAL ACCESS (Aptitude)

edges.notes: Hacking, surveillance, data access most cannot touch

data.creedFields:
CONCEPT
Still dragging a corkboard and a
dead K9 handler’s dog through
cases the department wants buried
-  and he’s rarely wrong about
what’s underneath.

play.ambition: Find the name behind the case that ended his career  -  the one that isn’t supposed to exist on paper  -  and finally make it stick to something real.
play.desire: Close this case clean, for once, without anyone else paying for what he didn’t catch in time.
play.touchstones:
PRYIA CHEN
The hacker friend, known for years. One of maybe two
people he trusts without reservation. She has stopped
asking follow-up questions, which worries him more than
if she pushed.

BISHOP
Not a warm dog. Trained, controlled, present. Since
Rosa’s death he alerts on things in no K9 manual  -  a
flat, dead stillness aimed at a person or a room. He is
never wrong.

DARA SILVA
Rosa’s younger sister. The official story never sat
right with her either. Ezekiel checks in on her more
than he would admit.
play.notes:
Player: Ibra
Humanity 7 - Health 5 - Willpower 5
Desperation and Danger are tracked per cell,
not per character.

TONE
Worn-down conviction, gallows humour; a man
who ran out of capacity for surprise a long
time ago and kept working anyway.
play.history:
Fourteen years on the force, mostly homicide, and Ezekiel was good at it  -  not flashy, just relentless. He didn’t let go of threads other detectives filed and forgot. That is what got him: a string of deaths written up as unrelated  -  overdoses, accidents, one ruled suicide he still doesn’t believe. He pulled the thread anyway and found all of them connected to a name that kept not existing on paper. His captain told him to drop it. He didn’t. Six months later he was out. Official story: conduct unbecoming. Unofficial story: somebody above his pay grade didn’t want the questions asked.

He has run his own PI shop since, taking the cases nobody else wants  -  missing persons that don’t add up, deaths closed too fast, families who know something is wrong and can’t get anyone in a uniform to listen. He has a corkboard that would make a task force uncomfortable, red string included, and he is right often enough that it has stopped being funny.

He smokes constantly. Not really for the nicotine  -  for the ritual. Lighting up is punctuation: the two seconds he allows himself between finding out something terrible and having to do something about it.
